title: To expand the sharing of information with respect to suspected violations of intellectual property rights in trade.

claims.claim: Under current law CBP can already ask parties to help identify suspected intellectual property rights violations, but only certain information can be shared (the premise this bill expands).
claims.sourceSpan: To expand the sharing of information with respect to suspected violations of intellectual property rights in trade.
claims.note: Framing consistent with the bill being an expansion amendment to 19 U.S.C. 1628a; the title states the purpose is to 'expand the sharing of information'.

claims.claim: The requesting parties are referred to as 'brand owners'.
claims.sourceSpan: To expand the sharing of information with respect to suspected violations of intellectual property rights in trade.
claims.note: Plain-English gloss for the intellectual-property-rights holders who request CBP assistance; grounded in the bill's stated IP-rights subject, but not named verbatim in the amendment text (subsection (b)'s existing recipient list is not shown in the Engrossed diff).

claims.claim: This bill lets CBP share nonpublic data generated by online marketplaces, freight forwarders, and express consignment operators.
claims.sourceSpan: may provide to the person nonpublic information about the merchandise that was generated by an online marketplace or other similar market platform, express consignment operator, freight forwarder, or any other entity that plays a role in the sale or importation of merchandise, or the facilitation thereof, into the United States that has been provided to, shared with, or obtained by U.S. Customs and Border Protection
claims.note: All three entity types appear verbatim (singular) in new paragraph (3).

claims.claim: Sharing can go to any other party the Commissioner determines has an interest in the merchandise.
claims.sourceSpan: any other party with an interest in the merchandise, as determined appropriate by the Commissioner
claims.note: Verbatim in new paragraph (5) added to subsection (b).

claims.claim: Broadens shareable physical evidence to include packing materials and containers.
claims.sourceSpan: by inserting ``, packing materials, containers,'' after ``its packaging'' the first place it appears
claims.note: Engrossed text says 'containers' (not 'shipping containers' — the stale analysis carried the Introduced wording; corrected).

claims.claim: Requires CBP to notify the recipient of any nonpublic information it transmits.
claims.sourceSpan: in the case of the provision of nonpublic information described in paragraph (3), shall provide to the person notification of the information transmitted, in accordance with such regulations as the Secretary may prescribe
claims.note: New paragraph (4) in the Engrossed text; absent from the stale (Introduced-based) analysis, now added.

claims.claim: Expands what counterfeit-goods intelligence CBP can share with brand owners.
claims.sourceSpan: To expand the sharing of information with respect to suspected violations of intellectual property rights in trade.
claims.note: 'counterfeit-goods intelligence' and 'brand owners' are plain-English glosses for information about suspected IP-rights violations and the IP-rights holders; grounded in the bill's stated subject, not verbatim entities.

claims.claim: Adds marketplace and freight data, packing materials, and a broader circle of eligible recipients.
claims.sourceSpan: may provide to the person nonpublic information about the merchandise that was generated by an online marketplace or other similar market platform, express consignment operator, freight forwarder
claims.note: Marketplace/freight data = para (3); packing materials = (a)(1); broader recipients = (b)(5).

claims.claim: CBP can now share nonpublic data from online marketplaces, freight forwarders, and express consignment operators with brand owners.
claims.sourceSpan: may provide to the person nonpublic information about the merchandise that was generated by an online marketplace or other similar market platform, express consignment operator, freight forwarder, or any other entity that plays a role in the sale or importation of merchandise
claims.note: Entity types verbatim in para (3); 'brand owners' is the plain-English recipient gloss (minor).

claims.claim: Packing materials and containers added to physical evidence that can be shared.
claims.sourceSpan: inserting ``, its packaging, packing materials, containers, and labels''
claims.note: 'containers' verbatim; packaging and labels pre-existed (struck and re-inserted), so the net additions are packing materials and containers.

claims.claim: CBP must notify the recipient of nonpublic information it transmits.
claims.sourceSpan: shall provide to the person notification of the information transmitted, in accordance with such regulations as the Secretary may prescribe
claims.note: New paragraph (4); 'the recipient' = 'the person' who receives the info under para (3).

claims.claim: Adds 'any other party with an interest in the merchandise' as an eligible recipient, at the Commissioner's discretion.
claims.sourceSpan: any other party with an interest in the merchandise, as determined appropriate by the Commissioner
claims.note: Quoted phrase verbatim; 'at the Commissioner's discretion' paraphrases 'as determined appropriate by the Commissioner'.

claims.claim: Standard for sharing changed from 'suspects' to 'has a reasonable suspicion'.
claims.sourceSpan: striking ``suspects'' and inserting ``has a reasonable suspicion''
claims.note: Both terms verbatim; stated neutrally as 'changed' (source strikes one and inserts the other) rather than making an unsourced raise/lower polarity claim.

claims.claim: Section 1 — Expansion of CBP Information Sharing.
claims.sourceSpan: SECTION 1. SHARING OF INFORMATION WITH RESPECT TO SUSPECTED VIOLATIONS OF INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY RIGHTS.
claims.note: Single-section bill; label reflects the section heading.

claims.claim: Amends Section 628A(a) of the Tariff Act of 1930 (19 U.S.C. 1628a) to authorize CBP to share nonpublic information generated by online marketplaces, express consignment operators, freight forwarders, and other importation-chain entities with parties requesting assistance in identifying IP violations.
claims.sourceSpan: Section 628A of the Tariff Act of 1930 (19 U.S.C. 1628a) is amended-- (1) in subsection (a)--
claims.note: Statutory cite and subsection (a) verbatim; entity list and 'any other entity ... in the sale or importation' verbatim in para (3).

claims.claim: CBP may provide a requesting party with nonpublic information about the merchandise generated by an online marketplace or similar platform, express consignment operator, freight forwarder, or any other entity involved in the sale, importation, or facilitation of the merchandise into the United States, provided that information was provided to, shared with, or obtained by CBP.
claims.sourceSpan: may provide to the person nonpublic information about the merchandise that was generated by an online marketplace or other similar market platform, express consignment operator, freight forwarder, or any other entity that plays a role in the sale or importation of merchandise, or the facilitation thereof, into the United States that has been provided to, shared with, or obtained by U.S. Customs and Border Protection
claims.note: Close paraphrase of paragraph (3); 'provided to, shared with, or obtained by' verbatim.

claims.claim: In the case of such a provision, CBP must notify the person of the information transmitted, in accordance with regulations the Secretary may prescribe.
claims.sourceSpan: in the case of the provision of nonpublic information described in paragraph (3), shall provide to the person notification of the information transmitted, in accordance with such regulations as the Secretary may prescribe
claims.note: New paragraph (4), added during reconciliation to the Engrossed text.

claims.claim: The scope of shareable physical evidence expands to include packing materials and containers, in addition to the merchandise and its packaging.
claims.sourceSpan: by inserting ``, packing materials, containers,'' after ``its packaging'' the first place it appears
claims.note: 'containers' verbatim (corrected from stale 'shipping containers'); 'its packaging' verbatim.

claims.claim: The standard for initiating the sharing is changed from 'suspects' to 'has a reasonable suspicion'.
claims.sourceSpan: striking ``suspects'' and inserting ``has a reasonable suspicion''
claims.note: Neutral 'changed'; removed the stale 'trademark or copyright law' characterization (unsourced) — the text says only 'intellectual property rights'.

claims.claim: Expands the class of parties eligible to receive CBP information to any party with an interest in the merchandise, as determined appropriate by the Commissioner.
claims.sourceSpan: any other party with an interest in the merchandise, as determined appropriate by the Commissioner
claims.note: Verbatim from new paragraph (5).

claims.claim: The bill adds a new paragraph (5) to Section 628A(b) — which lists the parties eligible to receive shared information — allowing the Commissioner to extend access to any other party with an interest in the merchandise.
claims.sourceSpan: in subsection (b)-- (A) in paragraph (3), by striking ``; and'' and inserting a semicolon; (B) in paragraph (4), by striking the period at the end and inserting ``; and''; and (C) by adding at the end the following: ``(5) any other party with an interest in the merchandise, as determined appropriate by the Commissioner.''
claims.note: Structure verbatim: (5) added to subsection (b) after existing paragraphs (3)/(4); '(b) lists eligible parties' is a structural inference from adding a party to that list. Removed the stale 'current law limits the program to trademark or copyright owners' claim (about the unfetched underlying statute, unsourced).

claims.claim: No statutory definition of 'interest' or limit on the Commissioner's discretion to determine eligibility is provided.
claims.sourceSpan: any other party with an interest in the merchandise, as determined appropriate by the Commissioner
claims.note: Absence-based: the text grants the discretion with no definition or constraint in the bill.

claims.claim: Section 628A(a)(3) — CBP authority to share nonpublic information generated by online marketplaces, express consignment operators, freight forwarders, and other importation-chain entities with parties assisting in IP violation determinations.
claims.sourceSpan: ``(3) may provide to the person nonpublic information about the merchandise that was generated by an online marketplace or other similar market platform, express consignment operator, freight forwarder, or any other entity that plays a role in the sale or importation of merchandise
claims.note: New paragraph (3).

claims.claim: Section 628A(a)(4) — CBP must notify the person of nonpublic information transmitted under paragraph (3), in accordance with regulations the Secretary may prescribe.
claims.sourceSpan: ``(4) in the case of the provision of nonpublic information described in paragraph (3), shall provide to the person notification of the information transmitted, in accordance with such regulations as the Secretary may prescribe
claims.note: New paragraph (4); added during reconciliation.

claims.claim: Section 628A(b)(5) — Commissioner authority to share information with any other party with an interest in the merchandise.
claims.sourceSpan: ``(5) any other party with an interest in the merchandise, as determined appropriate by the Commissioner
claims.note: New paragraph (5) added to subsection (b).

claims.claim: Section 628A(a) sharing threshold changed from 'suspects' to 'has a reasonable suspicion' of an intellectual property rights violation.
claims.sourceSpan: in the matter preceding paragraph (1), by striking ``suspects'' and inserting ``has a reasonable suspicion''
claims.note: 'suspects' and 'has a reasonable suspicion' verbatim; 'intellectual property rights' from the title/heading (replaced stale 'trademark or copyright').

claims.claim: Section 628A(a)(1) — physical evidence shareable with requesting parties expanded to include packing materials and containers.
claims.sourceSpan: by inserting ``, packing materials, containers,'' after ``its packaging''
claims.note: 'expanded to include' matches the source's insertion; 'containers' verbatim (corrected from 'shipping containers').

claims.claim: Section 1(2)(C) — Open-Ended Recipient Class.
claims.sourceSpan: (C) by adding at the end the following: ``(5) any other party with an interest in the merchandise, as determined appropriate by the Commissioner.''
claims.note: The (2)(C) amendment adds paragraph (5); anchor resolves to the Engrossed structure.

claims.claim: The bill extends information sharing to 'any other party with an interest in the merchandise, as determined appropriate by the Commissioner'; no statutory definition of 'interest' is provided and the Commissioner's authority to determine who qualifies is unconstrained by the bill.
claims.sourceSpan: any other party with an interest in the merchandise, as determined appropriate by the Commissioner
claims.note: Quoted phrase verbatim; the 'no definition / unconstrained' observation is absence-based.

claims.claim: The bill's stated purpose is expanding information sharing about suspected intellectual property rights violations; paragraph (5) extends sharing to any party the Commissioner deems interested — a category that could include competitors of the importer, brokers, or other commercial parties not directly harmed by the alleged violation.
claims.sourceSpan: any other party with an interest in the merchandise, as determined appropriate by the Commissioner
claims.note: Purpose clause sourced from title/heading; 'competitors/brokers' are illustrative examples of the open-ended category, not named in source (analysis, not fabricated fact).

claims.claim: The bill authorizes sharing of nonpublic information generated by online marketplaces and freight operators but does not specify what categories of nonpublic data are covered or excluded.
claims.sourceSpan: may provide to the person nonpublic information about the merchandise that was generated by an online marketplace or other similar market platform, express consignment operator, freight forwarder
claims.note: Bill-anchored gap: paragraph (3) authorizes 'nonpublic information' with no category scoping in the text.

claims.claim: The bill does not address the rights of the importer or the source entity (e.g., the online marketplace) to receive notice that their nonpublic information has been shared with a third party.
claims.sourceSpan: shall provide to the person notification of the information transmitted, in accordance with such regulations as the Secretary may prescribe
claims.note: Gap remains valid under the Engrossed text: paragraph (4) requires notice only to 'the person' (the recipient), not to the importer or source entity.

claims.claim: The bill has bipartisan sponsorship (Moore R-UT and Schneider D-IL) and 6 cosponsors.
claims.note: Structural metadata (sponsor party, cosponsor count) — not derived from bill text; permitted in Zone 3. No bill-text span.

claims.claim: Anti-counterfeiting measures attract broad support.
claims.note: Breadth-of-support characterization not tied to a recorded vote or any source; left as visible style debt per the rubric (framing flags stay open). Prose not changed during this reconciliation.

claims.claim: billType = amendment.
claims.sourceSpan: Section 628A of the Tariff Act of 1930 (19 U.S.C. 1628a) is amended--
claims.note: Bill amends an existing statute (19 U.S.C. 1628a) via strike/insert; amendment classification holds.

resolution: Reconciled the stale (Introduced-based) analysis to the Engrossed (passed House 2026-04-27) text. Corrected 'shipping containers' -> 'containers' (summary, top_lines, sections, changes); added new paragraph (4) notification requirement (summary, top_lines, sections.detail, changes.added); replaced unsourced 'trademark or copyright' characterizations with the sourced 'intellectual property rights' and removed the unsourced 'current law limits the program to trademark or copyright owners' claim about the unfetched underlying statute; changed 'shipping operators' -> 'express consignment operators' and neutralized the 'raised' threshold wording to 'changed'. No material errors remain against the Engrossed text.
notes: No referencedSources registered; the Engrossed bill text is the sole source. One open framing flag on likelihoodReason ('broad support') kept as style debt. gaps[1] remains valid because para (4) notice runs to the recipient only, not the importer/source.
